guitar.evidence: Jimi Hendrix's white Fender Stratocaster (played upside-down/restrung for a right-handed guitar as a left-handed player) is one of the most iconic guitar associations in rock history.

tone.target: warm Hendrix clean-crunch with subtle fuzz and short room
tone.profile: warm Hendrix clean-crunch with subtle fuzz and short room
tone.summary: A classic, warm Fender-style clean foundation boosted by a Fuzz/OD stage, running through a Marshall-voiced amp model, finished with room reverb and vibrato.

rig.name: Jimi Hendrix - Castles Made Of Sand - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and stray noise inherent in vintage-style tones.
Provide the required 'slight fuzz breakup' and vintage grit (Fuzz Face style).

alternatives.reason: Good for early British rock, but 'Fuzz' is more direct for the Fuzz Face vibe.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle harmonic warmth and mid-range punch for the 'warm mids' requirement.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a general boost, but it helps shape the tone to avoid excessive scoop while maintaining clarity.

alternatives.reason: Might be too aggressive for the required 'slight' breakup.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall/Super Lead tone and provide classic British rock power.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative, but SLP better captures the Super Lead/Marshall vibe.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required '4x12' cabinet voicing for a classic British rock sound.
Fine-tune the tone to emphasize 'warm mids' and maintain fullness.
Achieve the 'expressive vibrato' required for lead lines.
Add the required 'short room verb' for space and sustain.

alternatives.reason: Room is better suited for a natural, short ambient decay.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and warmth by swapping the default 4x12 IR for a vintage, open-air British cab simulation.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage, open-air feel and warmth of the Marshall tone.
